figures.caption: Fig. 1: Comparison of baseline recursive chunking versus the proposed structure-aware framework. The baseline method (top) operates on linearized text with token-level splitting and overlap, which can fragment rows across multiple chunks and introduce redundant tokens. In contrast, the proposed framework (bottom) represents each row as a key-value (KV) block within a Row Tree hierarchy. By applying token-constrained splitting and greedy merging, the method produces dense, non-overlapping chunks aligned with row-level structure.
